study_identification_part.si4_title: Deep Normative Tractometry for Identifying Joint White Matter Macro- and Micro-structural Abnormalities in Alzheimer's Disease

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Propose and evaluate a Deep Normative Tractometry (DNT) framework based on a variational autoencoder trained on healthy controls to learn the normative distribution of along-tract macro- and micro-structural profiles, and assess generalizability via transfer learning to detect abnormalities in MCI and Alzheimer's disease.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The normative model was initially pre-trained on 198 healthy subjects from the TractoInferno dataset. Subsequently, 50 cognitively normal (CN) subjects from the NIMHANS dataset were used to fine-tune the model. The total number of healthy controls used for the normative model is the sum of these two groups (198 + 50 = 248).
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: The pre-training dataset was composed of 198 singleshell dMRI volumes from the publicly available TractoInferno training dataset [32]" and "Fifty CN subjects from the NIMHANS dataset, randomly selected and stratified by sex and scanner, were then used to fine-tune the model for 5000 steps.
rci2_hc_n.location: Feng2024.pdf.md: Section II. DATA, Paragraph 3 and Section III. METHOD, Paragraph 2
